finalists.label: Legionnaires' disease
finalists.why: Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine and right-sided lung infiltrates strongly support this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Pneumonia
finalists.why: Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine and right-sided lung infiltrates are also consistent with pneumonia, but Legionnaires' disease is a more specific diagnosis.

finalists.label: Cardiogenic shock
finalists.why: LVEF 50% and moderate subendocardial LGE in multiple segments suggest cardiac involvement, but cardiogenic shock is not directly supported by the evidence.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine specifically supports Legionnaires' disease over pneumonia.
